summary: Better: keep d1f1caa3f7 and a835f03e6f. Network-denied Task status falls 59.1% with one capacity read, then 61.5% with one scope resolution per repository. Five alternating pairs per comparison; non-overlapping primary ranges, matching full JSON and zero command or validation errors.

notes.attribution: Native samples put Keychain reads at 62.2% before and 2.2% after capacity reuse. Five separate count runs per side/workload record exactly 336 → 4 → 4 security spawns per Task call; Session list stays at four and Wave/board at zero. The scope wall-timer run records 1,154 → 40 repository_scope calls, 1,508.7 → 16.7 ms. Both SQL traces execute 3,812 statements with the same leading work counters; no SQL speedup is attributed to scope caching.
notes.arithmetic: Capacity removes 98.8% of security spawns from a path occupying about 62.2% of baseline samples: an approximate 61.5% ceiling is consistent with the 59.1% cohort reduction. For scope, the separately profiled complete check takes 1,560.7 of 2,662.7 ms (58.6%): deleting it permits at most a 58.6% latency reduction, or 2.42× speed. Its candidate takes 43.2 ms in a 1,125.1 ms command: a 57.7% path reduction, within that bound. The check saves 1,517.6 ms of the command’s 1,537.6 ms reduction (98.7%). Nested scope time is not added. These are bounds for the instrumented runs; the uninstrumented 61.5% cohort reduction was measured in different runs and is not numerically decomposed by those timers. Native stack shares cover captured samples, not the complete elapsed command.
notes.next_limiter: Next limiter: planning field delivery repeatedly resolves repository identity. The final native sample has 204/578 main-thread samples (35.3%) in RepoId::discover; the separate wall-timer run makes 28 discoveries taking 318.9 ms of 1,125.1 ms (28.3%). Path: linear_observe::sync_scope → planning_delivery::deliver_fields → PlanningClient::for_repository → linear::resolve_repository_context → RepoId::discover → git remote get-url origin. Eliminating all discovery time would cap that run’s gain at 28.3% latency, or about 1.40× speed. SQL is another remaining cost: the final trace’s leading Process query takes 112.7 ms across five executions; the final native sample has 29.8% in sqlite3_step. These nested/profile measures are not added. No next optimization was made.
notes.limits: Same sealed iteration-2 store (14,759 Sessions, 236,791 events, 160,314 Processes, 1,099 Tasks, six accounts), identical standalone files and 78 application-table digests. No fresh live-store backup; every benchmark uses /tmp/loo822-reads-measure via LF_HOME, never the live ~/.lf store. Exact commit exports, identical release build flags, Rust 1.98.1, macOS 26.0.1 arm64; all builds finished before their measurements. The unchanged five timing-harness hashes match iteration 2. One excluded warm-up per call; fixed wall clock, warm filesystem state, unchanged private provider transcript copies without credential files. OS processes, Git/config files and Keychain fallback behavior remain ambient; timed one-minute load ranged 10.0–26.6. Network rejection is intentional and does not measure successful exchange or online authentication. The unreproduced 18–75 s stall remains open.
